data.title: Thiabendazole (oral + topical)
data.summary: Other antiparasitics · Benzimidazole anthelmintic (first of its class)
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Other antiparasitics_

**Class:** Benzimidazole anthelmintic (first of its class)

## Mechanism of action
- Inhibits helminth fumarate reductase and microtubule function; also anti-inflammatory and antipyretic

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Topical 10–15% (suspension/cream, compounded, or crushed tablets in petrolatum): cutaneous larva migrans — applied to the track and 2 cm beyond
- Oral: strongyloidiasis, CLM, visceral larva migrans (now replaced by ivermectin/albendazole; oral form withdrawn in many countries)

## Dose & formulations
- Topical: 10–15% three times daily for 5 days (or until track stops progressing)
- Oral (historic): 25 mg/kg twice daily for 2–5 days (max 3 g/day)

## Adverse effects
- Oral: frequent nausea, vomiting, dizziness, foul-smelling urine, hepatotoxicity, SJS/TEN, hallucinations
- Topical: minimal irritation

## Contraindications
- Oral: liver disease, pregnancy

## Drug interactions
- Oral: raises theophylline levels

## Pregnancy & lactation
Topical acceptable; avoid oral.

## Viva points
- Topical thiabendazole for localised CLM (useful in children and pregnancy)
- Oral form largely abandoned because of side effects

_Sources: Khopkar ch.5 and ch.21; Wolverton 4e ch.12 and ch.44. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
